scope: Proposition 2.6 (Equal-type transport) of the manuscript “A negative solution to the finite lattice representation problem” (preprints/A-Negative-Solution-to-the-Finite-Lattice-Representation-Problem-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 206 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a102efd4a3009423), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 8. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let D < X < Y be labelled vertices. Then FY ≤ FX, and TX is isomorphic to a section of TY . Put EX = (X ∩ NY )/FY ≤ SY . The following conditions are equivalent: (i) TX ∼ = TY ; (ii) EX is subdirect in SY . When they hold, the quotient map induces an isomorphism EX ∼ − − → SX, NX = FX(X ∩ NY ), FX ∩ NY = FY . (2.4) Moreover mX < mY , and the strip supports give a canonical X-equivariant surjection σY X : IY −→ IX. (2.5) For three comparable labelled vertices of the same simple type these maps compose: σZX = σY XσZY .
